subject: Fix system stack retaining closed TCP sessions
root_cause: The system stack's TCP session/NAT table kept a session after the app-side connection had closed, because nothing deleted it on the close path, so closed sessions lingered until a timeout sweep and their mapping could still be matched; sing-tun deletes the session when the connection closes.
fork_evidence: Same sing-tun pin (go.mod:58 require 9ffa5391a2ad, :354 replace 109186a15f3b); upstream fix 84e75a655a43 is later than the fork's base and absent from the fork's sing-tun history. In the fork's copy the only removal is the LastActive timeout sweep, stack_system_nat.go:54-84 (checkTimeout deletes addrMap/portMap when expired), with no close-time delete.
notes: Timeout-only removal means a closed session keeps its mapping for the full NAT timeout and can be revived by a late packet. Check whether 84e75a655a43 adds a close-path delete; if so, backport it into the Piggy-Cat-bit-shadow sing-tun fork.

subject: Fix Apple TLS engine connection leak
root_cause: Apple TLS leaked per handshake: the dup'd socket fd was created before CA resolution so error returns never closed it; client creation ran outside an autorelease pool on a Go thread (autoreleased NSArray/NSDate/nw_parameters leak); and the dlsym'd nw_connection_create returns +1 but was declared without NW_RETURNS_RETAINED, so ARC over-retained each connection and its fd. The fix moves/CLOEXECs the dup, defers anchors.Release, wraps create in a pool and annotates the typedef.
fork_evidence: common/tls/apple_client_platform.go:48 unix.Dup before :65 resolveAnchors (error return leaks dupFD), :99 non-deferred anchors.Release; apple_client_platform_darwin.m:17 typedef lacks NW_RETURNS_RETAINED and :356 box_apple_tls_client_create has no @autoreleasepool although other functions do.
notes: Leak grows with every TLS connection (fd plus nw_connection object) until exhaustion. No F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC appears anywhere in the fork.

subject: Fix WireGuard pause and sleep handling
root_cause: ClientBind waited on the pause manager with the uncancellable WaitActive() plus a bare time.Sleep, from both wireguard-go's receive and send goroutines, so while the network was paused the receive loop (and device.Close waiting on it) could not be torn down; and the pause callbacks drove device Up/Down from the event type alone without re-reading the pause state, so a late or reordered event could leave the device down after a wake.
fork_evidence: Endpoint half is already owned differently: endpoint.go:799-816 keeps networkPaused under stateAccess, :717-769 closes the device under the same lock. Bind half is not: client_bind.go:96-104 still calls pauseManager.WaitActive(), used at :211 (receive) and :282 (Send); :256-267 sleepRetry is a bare time.Sleep; WaitActiveContext appears nowhere in the tree.
notes: Needs a context-aware wait in the sing fork first (its pause.Manager still has WaitActive only; fake at pause_deadlock_test.go:104 shows the interface). Endpoint.Close holds stateAccess across device.Close, which turns the stuck receive into a teardown stall against every pause callback; also drop the WaitActive from Send.

subject: Fix TUN flow table retaining accepted TCP connections
root_cause: In the pinned sing-tun the TUN flow table kept the entry for a TCP flow that had been accepted out of the stack, because the accept/handoff path did not release or re-key the entry, so the table grew with every accepted connection and stale flow state stayed reachable; fixed in the sing-tun revision.
fork_evidence: Dependency sync: the sing-tun pin now includes baaa611 (accepted TCP flow entries removed after handshake); `go test ./protocol/tun` and `go build ./...` pass. Upstream: 03ab009ea1c0.
notes: Fixed in this round; see docs/fork/upstream-2026-10-24-debug.md.

subject: Fix network namespace with TCP Fast Open
root_cause: With TCP Fast Open the real connect is deferred to the first Write of a slowOpenConn; that deferred dial ran after the netns wrapper had already returned, so the socket was created in the host namespace and the configured netns was ignored.
fork_evidence: Port in this round: DialSlowContext carries the namespace and the deferred TFO dial enters it via listener.ListenNetworkNamespace. Build + `./common/dialer` tests pass. Upstream: 8e90fc34e6e8.
notes: Fixed in this round; see docs/fork/upstream-2026-10-24-debug.md.

subject: Fix flow close racing with tracker attach
root_cause: multiFlowTracker was a bare slice, so AttachFlow (accept path) and CloseFlow (flow teardown) could run concurrently for one flow. They raced on flowInterrupter.removers - append versus iterate - and a close could miss a handle attached after it, leaking the group registration and the close notification.
fork_evidence: Port in this round: `multiFlowTracker` is a locked struct; AttachFlow and CloseFlow are serialized, the counters stay lock-free. Test: `route/flow_tracker_serialization_test.go`. Upstream: 92fe54be05f2.
notes: Fixed in this round; see docs/fork/upstream-2026-10-24-debug.md.

subject: Fix TUN loopback protection for ICMP
root_cause: For ICMP the direct outbound takes the flow path (PreMatchFlow then WritePackets into the ping port) and never ran the isMyLoopbackAddress guard that DialContext/ListenPacket apply; an echo to an address inside the TUN's own prefixes was written back into the TUN, re-entered routing and looped.
fork_evidence: Port in this round: `protocol/direct` rejects an ICMP flow to the TUN's own range. Test: `protocol/direct/icmp_loopback_test.go`. Upstream: b722a038e61b.
notes: Fixed in this round; see docs/fork/upstream-2026-10-24-debug.md.

subject: Fix QUIC Chrome parrot packet size on IPv6
root_cause: Chrome-parrot pinned its Initial packet at 1250 bytes (Chrome's IPv4 value). IPv6 adds 20 header bytes, so on a 1280-byte IPv6 path the datagram needs 1298 bytes and is dropped, stalling the QUIC handshake. quic-go mod.11 sets InitialPacketSize to 1230 when the remote address is IPv6.
fork_evidence: go.mod:46 requires sagernet/quic-go mod.9, replaced at go.mod:297 by Piggy-Cat-bit-shadow/quic-go v0.61.1-0.20261019061042; its chrome_parrot.go:19 still has chromeInitialPacketSize=1250 with no IPv6 variant and transport.go:258-260 only sets the Initial packet number. Its InitialPacketSizeCeiling is applied after ChromeParrot, but only hysteria2 sets it and only for a known detour path.
notes: Upstream mod.11 diff adds chromeInitialPacketSizeIPv6=1230 and applies it in Transport.dial when the remote Is6. Cherry-pick those lines into the quic-go fork or set the ceiling for direct IPv6; otherwise hysteria2 ChromeParrot can fail on minimum-MTU IPv6 paths.

subject: Fix QUIC and UDP sessions closing on EMSGSIZE
root_cause: Oversized datagrams make a connected UDP read or write return EMSGSIZE (ICMP frag-needed / packet-too-big). The packet copy loops treated it as fatal, so one oversized packet tore down QUIC and Hysteria2 sessions. Upstream fixes this only inside dependencies: sing-quic ignores EMSGSIZE in the hop receive loop, and sing bufio drops the oversized packet and continues instead of ending the copy loop.
fork_evidence: Fork pins its own forks: go.mod:212 sing v0.9.6-0.20261019051552-baed8c3b4a34, go.mod:297 quic-go v0.61.1-0.20261019061042-7e08ecaba383, go.mod:307 sing-quic v0.7.2-0.20261019060901-d0deb0359c06. Those trees have no errMessageTooLong handling in common/bufio and no EMSGSIZE skip in hysteria/hop.go; the fork has no local workaround either.
notes: Upstream: quic-go v0.61.0-sing-box-mod.9 -> mod.10; sing v0.9.7-0.20261020035405-749ff46463b3 -> v0.9.7-0.20261023115459-226df7434a64; sing-quic v0.7.2-0.20261002084117-75c3ac4fa12b -> v0.7.2-0.20261020082049-7e0a5869a5f4. subject: Fix interface binding for dual-stack sockets on Windows
root_cause: On Windows, bindToInterface treated every non-'4' network as IPv6 and set only IPV6_UNICAST_IF. Go dials 'tcp'/'udp' as dual-stack AF_INET6 sockets (IPV6_V6ONLY=0), where IPV6_UNICAST_IF does not steer IPv4 traffic and fails with WSAEADDRNOTAVAIL when the interface has IPv6 disabled, so IPv4 over dual-stack sockets was unbound or failed. The fix checks IPV6_V6ONLY and also applies IP_UNICAST_IF.
fork_evidence: go.mod:212 replaces sagernet/sing with Piggy-Cat-bit-shadow/sing v0.9.6-0.20261019051552-baed8c3b4a34 (2026-10-19), whose common/control/bind_windows.go still has the pre-fix 'default: return bind6(...)' branch and the address-empty special case; the IPV6_V6ONLY/IP_UNICAST_IF logic from upstream sing 237e23f25bb1 is absent.
notes: Cherry-pick upstream sing's bind_windows.go change into the sing fork or bump the pin; affects network_strategy/bind_interface on Windows dual-stack sockets, including IPv4 dials over AF_INET6 sockets.

subject: Apply backpressure to masque inbound packets
root_cause: Masque session read loops pushed received inner packets into the memory TUN through the non-blocking WritePackets, which silently drops when the stack's inbound ring is full; nothing waited for room, so the peer's QUIC flow-control window never learned about the loss and TCP-in-MASQUE lost packets instead of slowing the sender.
fork_evidence: transport/device/device.go:20-34 Device has only WriteInboundBuffers; transport/device/stack.go:72-79 writes via memoryTun.WritePackets; transport/masque/client.go:680 and server.go:549 still call WriteInboundBuffers. Pinned sing-tun (go.mod:354) tun_memory.go:119-121 silently 'continue's when the ring is full; no WaitWritePackets exists in the tree.
notes: Needs a wait/wake API in the memory TUN (upstream added WaitWritePackets in sing-tun). Without it, add a bounded blocking writer to the device and use it only on the masque inbound path, keeping the drop policy for the lossy outbound queue.

subject: Fix network strategy for ICMP
root_cause: ICMP ping sockets took their creation control from dialer4/dialer6, chosen only by destination family. Those base dialers carry auto-detect/protect/mark controls but not the network_strategy/network_type interface selection, which lives in the parallel/serial dial paths, so ICMP probes ignored the configured strategy and left by the default interface (or failed on multi-homed/Android setups). The fix derives one strategy-aware interface control for ICMP.
fork_evidence: common/dialer/default.go:518-524 DialerForICMPDestination returns dialer4/dialer6 by family and ignores d.networkStrategy/networkType; protocol/direct/outbound.go:110-112 hands that Control to ping.NewPort; the strategy interface binding lives only in DialParallelInterface/listenSerialInterfacePacket (common/dialer/default_parallel_interface.go:193-235).
notes: Port needs a control.Func equivalent of upstream's serialInterfaceControl (the sing fork already has BindToInterface0) plus default-strategy EPERM tolerance; protocol/direct is the only consumer.

subject: Fix connection owner lookup on legacy Android
root_cause: Legacy Android (SDK<Q) falls back to scanning /proc/net for the connection UID. The scan matched only local_address in the single-stack table, ignored remote port and inode, and never tried tcp6, so dual-stack AF_INET6 Java sockets (IPv4 flows appear only in tcp6 as v4-mapped) and UDP wildcard/listener rows were mis-resolved. Upstream moves the scan to an exported Android-only helper with table fallback, remote matching and UDP ranking.
fork_evidence: experimental/libbox/internal/procfs/procfs.go:33 keeps ResolveSocketByProcSearch(network, source, _ netip.AddrPort) matching local_address only (no rem_address/inode columns). service.go:195-214 still gates on UseProcFS; platform.go:10 still declares it; only connection_owner_darwin.go exists. clients/android .../PlatformInterfaceWrapper.kt:56 useProcFS = SDK_INT < Q.
notes: Upstream deletes PlatformInterface.UseProcFS and adds connection_owner_android.go. Port requires the libbox change plus switching the Android client from useProcFS to Libbox.findConnectionOwner.

subject: Fix IPv6 literal host handling
root_cause: Several request URLs/Host headers were built by concatenating a host that may be an IPv6 literal. Without brackets, 'https://2001:db8::1' parses as host '2001' with port 'db8::1', so DoH/HTTP3/DERP mesh and v2ray HTTP requests dial the wrong address or fail; in REALITY fallback the NewRequest error was discarded, leaving a nil request that panics on Header.Set. The fix brackets IPv6 literals via the sockaddr parser and returns the error.
fork_evidence: dns/transport/https.go:74-93 and dns/transport/quic/http3.go:72-91 build url.URL from an unbracketed host; service/derp/service.go:351-361 uses hostname unbracketed for port 443; transport/v2rayhttp/client.go:117 sets Host to AddrString; transport/v2rayhttpupgrade/client.go:43 uses tlsConfig.ServerName raw; common/tls/reality_client.go:351 builds 'https://'+serverName, discards the error, then dereferences request.
notes: Upstream also bundles the http3 SetNextProtos(h3)/TLSClientConfig change and derp SetURLDialer using server.Server; check those when porting. The REALITY nil-request path is a config-triggered crash.

subject: Fix DHCP DNS search domain expansion
root_cause: DHCP built candidates from dns.FqdnToDomain(question.Name), which drops the root dot, so its rooted-name short-circuit never fired; with ndots=1 every already-qualified dotted name was also expanded against every DHCP search suffix (www.example.com.<search>), producing bogus upstream queries once the real name NXDOMAINs. The fix expands only single-label names and keeps the plain name last.

notes: The same expander also lives in local/systemconfig and the resolved service (next commit). Minimal fix: only expand when mDNS.CountLabel(name)==1, and validate the question name separately.

subject: Fix tailscale short name and DNS route matching
root_cause: Tailscale DNS route lookup ranged over the routes map, so overlapping suffixes resolved randomly and resolver-less local routes were not distinct from forwarded ones: a local name could be forwarded upstream or a forwarded name NXDOMAINed by map order. PreferredDomain treated any single-label name as tailnet-owned whenever a search domain existed, without checking the expansion. The fix adds a canonical matcher with local/forwarded suffixes, longest-first order and search-domain expansion.
fork_evidence: protocol/tailscale/dns_transport.go:349-368 PreferredDomain ranges over routes and returns true for any single-label name; :474-500 exchangeOnce ranges over the routes map and distinguishes local only by len(transports)==0; endpoint.go:950-970 and :1004-1017 keep routeDomains, unsorted routeSuffixes and a searchDomains bool. No tailnetDomains type exists.
notes: Restores Tailscale's local-route NXDOMAIN semantics and MagicDNS short-name preference; otherwise LAN single-label names can be captured by tailscale and local names can leak to forwarded resolvers.

subject: Fix unshare network namespace with capabilities
root_cause: When CAP_SYS_ADMIN was missing but other capabilities were held, runInUserNamespaceIfNeeded re-executed into a rootless user namespace whose mapping leaves the child without the parent's caps, so the service lost NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW (or other granted caps) and netns/TUN setup failed without a clear cause. The fix rejects that combination with an explanatory error, adds NET_BIND_SERVICE to the ambient set, preserves the initial cwd, and makes the namespace holder ignore termination signals.
fork_evidence: cmd/sing-box/cmd_run_userns_linux.go:31-55 has no capability guard, no initialDir/command.Dir, and AmbientCaps lacks CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE; common/netns/netns.go:11-17 Hold() has no signal.Ignore; common/netns/manager_linux.go:115-119 still chooses nsenter advice by os.Geteuid()==0 and has no ownsUserNamespace/NS_GET_OWNER_UID.
notes: All four pieces are absent; port them together. The holder signal omission is a lifecycle issue: SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP can kill the holder and destroy the shared netns while sing-box still runs.

subject: Fix OOM killer staying triggered after reset
root_cause: The pressure state machine left pressureStateTriggered only when usage fell below a fourth resume threshold (limit minus 4x safety margin, or 4x margin of available), so after a reset released memory the state stayed triggered at the armed level; where 4x margin reaches the limit the resume threshold becomes 0 and the latch never clears. The fix removes the resume threshold so triggered exits at the armed level.
fork_evidence: The whole pre-fix shape is present: timer.go:47-51 resume field, :471-480 resume = limit - min(4*margin, limit), :448-469 passes usage >= resume as shouldStayTriggered, :608-622 latch exits only below resume; recorder.go:215/384 still emit resumeBytes; apple_policy_test.go:86-111 asserts resume < armed < trigger. Canonical 50MiB/5MiB policy gives resume 30MiB, so post-reset usage of 30-40MiB stays critical.
notes: Keep a resume notion for the releaseIdleMemory gate (timer.go:357 belowResume) if wanted; the state machine must exit triggered at the armed level and the recorder's resumeBytes field must go. Update apple_policy_test.go and the timer fixtures with the change.

subject: Flush systemd-resolved cache on DNS changes
root_cause: Clearing sing-box's in-process DNS cache does not invalidate systemd-resolved's cache: a link's cache is flushed only when its DNS server changes, which neither a network change nor a sing-box DNS reconfiguration does, so the OS resolver serves the old view until TTL. The fix adds NetworkManager.FlushSystemDNSCache, calls it from Router.ClearCache, resolved server-set updates and network-environment changes, and implements it via sing-tun's LinuxTUN.FlushDNSCache (resolvectl flush-caches).
fork_evidence: adapter/network.go:17-49 NetworkManager has no flush method (FlushSystemDNSCache is absent tree-wide); dns/router.go:2168-2193 ClearCache only clears the in-process client, platformInterface.ClearDNSCache and reverse mapping; route/network_environment.go:333-338 deliberately does not clear or flush; protocol/tun/inbound.go:793 InterfaceUpdated only resets the stack; the pinned sing-tun fork 109186a15f3b has no LinuxTUN.FlushDNSCache.
notes: Porting needs the sing-tun fork bumped to a revision carrying LinuxTUN.FlushDNSCache (upstream fba659785148) or a local resolvectl flush-caches call; skip when a resolved service owns DNS. Stale answers after DNS/network changes, no data loss.

subject: Fix systemd-resolved detection for local DNS server
root_cause: Detection scanned /etc/resolv.conf for a comment containing 'systemd-resolved'; a stub file without that comment (or written by another manager) made the D-Bus resolver be skipped, losing per-link DNS/DoT from resolved, while 127.0.0.53 from resolv.conf was treated as an ordinary server. Config carried no flag marking the servers as resolved-managed.
fork_evidence: dns/transport/local/local.go:77 still gates on isSystemdResolvedManaged(); local_resolved_linux.go:36-53 still scans /etc/resolv.conf comment lines; systemconfig/config.go:22-33 has no SystemdResolved and source_resolv.go:21 knows only /etc/resolv.conf; local.go:152 and :189 test t.resolved != nil alone; D-Bus calls pass flag 0, not dbus.FlagNoAutoStart (lines 469/587/735).
notes: Port: always attempt NewResolvedResolver when !preferGo, add Config.SystemdResolved (os.SameFile with /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf or listen addrs 127.0.0.53/.54) and consult it in Environment/ExchangeAsync; FlagNoAutoStart stops activating the unit.

subject: Remove unimplemented direct rule action
root_cause: action=direct was parsed and built into RuleActionDirect with a freshly created dialer, but nothing consumes it: matchRule dispatches only sniff/resolve and treats route/reject/hijack-dns/bypass as final, so a matched direct rule silently did nothing and matching continued, while reference collection counted it as final. Upstream removes the unimplemented action and its schema entry.
fork_evidence: route/rule/rule_action.go:76-96 builds RuleActionDirect with an unused Dialer (:400); option/rule_action.go:404 still emits it in routeActionUnion; constant/rule.go:37; route/route.go:1295-1330 handles sniff/resolve/route/reject/hijack/bypass but not direct; route/reference_rule.go:128 treats direct as final.
notes: Either delete the action (upstream) or implement direct dialing; until then configs using action=direct are accepted but silently ignored, so traffic can be routed by a later rule or the default outbound.

subject: Reject Tailscale SSH user switch without privilege
root_cause: On Unix verifyShellIdentity returned nil on the assumption that setCredential always drops to the requested user, so a switch the process cannot perform was only discovered later as an EPERM from fork/exec, and a root process stripped of CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID was never checked; the fix refuses the session up front unless the identity already matches or the switch capabilities are effective.
fork_evidence: protocol/tailscale/tailssh/server_helper_unix.go:24-27 is byte-identical to the upstream parent (build tag aside): verifyShellIdentity is a no-op. No switch_user_linux.go and no checkSwitchUserPrivilege exist under protocol/tailscale; the only Capget use in the tree is cmd/sing-box/cmd_run_userns_linux.go:27. Call sites: server.go:596 and :793.
notes: Today the effect is fail-closed (non-root setCredential fails at exec), so this is hardening plus a clear diagnostic rather than a proven escalation. Port verifyShellIdentity and a switch_user_linux/other pair, using the fork's with_tailscale build tag instead of upstream's with_gvisor.

subject: Check DNS address filter rules on cache hit
root_cause: Cache hits returned the stored answer before responseChecker ran, so an answer the address filter rejects was still served from cache; only freshly exchanged responses were checked, leaving the rule unenforced for cached data.
fork_evidence: dns/client.go:834-852 returns cached responses from beginExchange without calling responseChecker, and questionCache (:1332-1355) does the same; only finishExchange (:911-931) runs it. ErrResponseRejectedCached (:32) is used solely for the RDRC namespace (:897).
notes: Latent today because every production caller passes a nil checker (dns/router.go:1923, :1946, :2045), but the contract is broken for any future checker. Port: run responseChecker on both cache-hit sites and return ErrResponseRejectedCached with logRejectedResponse.

subject: Limit concurrent auto-redirect flow judgements
root_cause: JudgeFlow is a synchronous binder transaction into the app process and occupies one of its ~15 binder threads; every new auto-redirect flow produced an unbounded concurrent judgement, so a burst could exhaust the app's binder pool and block both the VPN read path and the system's calls into the app (hang/ANR).
fork_evidence: experimental/libbox/redirect_linux.go:99-111 autoRedirectServiceHandler has no limiter and JudgeFlow calls h.handler.JudgeFlow directly; the handler is built at :51 without any slot channel. No semaphore or channel bounds JudgeFlow anywhere in the tree.
notes: Port the 8-slot semaphore created in NewAutoRedirectService and taken/released around the binder call (release in a defer so a failing JudgeFlow cannot leak a slot).

subject: Fix shared connections inheriting external interrupt mark
root_cause: The external-connection mark was a one-way context value set on every routed flow, so contexts for shared transports (mux session, SSH client, gRPC/HTTP transport, snell reuse, DNS) inherited it. Those transports registered with a group's interrupt group as user connections, so an internal-only interrupt (selection change with interrupt_exist_connections unset) left them on the deselected member.
fork_evidence: Port in this round: the external-interrupt mark is a typed bool, explicit false for DNS/multiplex sessions and true for routed connections. Build + `./route`/`./dns` tests pass. Upstream: 0164ce7b8e0a.
notes: Fixed in this round; see docs/fork/upstream-2026-10-24-debug.md.

subject: Fix close handler skipped on packet handshake failure
root_cause: When N.ReportPacketConnHandshakeSuccess failed, the packet path closed both connections directly instead of calling N.CloseOnHandshakeFailure, so the registered onClose handler never ran: the group's interrupt registration, tracker state and manager bookkeeping for that flow were never released, and no linger or HandshakeFailure signal was sent.
fork_evidence: Port in this round: a packet handshake-success failure now goes through `CloseOnHandshakeFailure` and the close handler runs. Build + `./route` tests pass. Upstream: 37bddc915c02.
notes: Fixed in this round; see docs/fork/upstream-2026-10-24-debug.md.

subject: Fix IPv6 original destination port on big-endian
root_cause: The Linux IPv6 SO_ORIGINAL_DST branch byte-swapped the port (BigEndian.PutUint16 into a [2]byte, then LittleEndian.Uint16), correct only on little-endian hosts, so redirect inbounds on big-endian targets resolved a wrong destination port. Upstream deleted common/redir and moved to sing's control.GetOriginalDestination, dropping the darwin PF copy too.
fork_evidence: Port in this round: the IPv6 original-destination port is decoded from the sin6_port field in memory network order, fixing big-endian. `GOOS=linux go build ./common/redir` passes. Upstream: 6564c26d409b.
notes: Fixed in this round; see docs/fork/upstream-2026-10-24-debug.md.

subject: Fix Windows connection loop with weak host send
root_cause: Windows ignores IP_UNICAST_IF/IPV6_UNICAST_IF when the bound interface has weak host send enabled (Teredo enables it on every interface), so sockets bound to an interface are routed back into the TUN and connections loop. sing-tun now tracks interface changes, disables weak host send on the other interfaces while running, and restores it on close.
fork_evidence: Dependency sync: the sing-tun pin now includes 4faef97 (weak-host send interface binding); pin-only upstream commit. Upstream: 6ddf133d3490.
notes: Fixed in this round; see docs/fork/upstream-2026-10-24-debug.md.

subject: Fix tun platform interface checks
root_cause: Platform-interface presence was used as a proxy for 'the platform creates the TUN', but the interface can be non-nil while UsePlatformInterface() is false (Apple outside Network Extension, libbox config-check stub). GSO, flow/auto-redirect setup and route_address_set extraction were then skipped although sing-tun opens the device.

subject: Fix Android package name lookup
root_cause: On Android every app's /proc/<pid>/exe is the shared zygote binary /system/bin/app_process*, so the reported process path identifies no app and defeats package-name identification; and the all-users /proc fallback (which exists only for sockets whose creator uid differs from the process uid after a privilege drop) cannot help because netd already chowns app DNS sockets to the app uid, so each miss pays a full /proc scan.
fork_evidence: Port in this round: Android skips the app_process wrapper paths and the all-users scan; `GOOS=linux go build ./common/process` passes. Upstream: 79d2e8084ed1.
notes: Fixed in this round; see docs/fork/upstream-2026-10-24-debug.md.

subject: Fix process search for redirect inbound
root_cause: Redirect inbound set metadata.Destination from SO_ORIGINAL_DST but left metadata.OriginDestination at the value the TCP listener stored (the local REDIRECT target). Process search prefers a valid OriginDestination, so it looked up the redirect address instead of the real original destination and never found the process.
fork_evidence: Port in this round: `protocol/redirect` populates `OriginDestination` (delivered in the previous commit). Upstream: 7f1a439ff069.
notes: Fixed in this round; see docs/fork/upstream-2026-10-24-debug.md.

subject: Fix tls spoof raw socket routing on Linux
root_cause: Linux routes IP_HDRINCL raw packets by the raw socket's bound device, SO_MARK and bound source (raw_sendmsg), not by the addresses inside the supplied header. The spoofer opened an unbound raw socket, so injected ClientHello segments followed the main table, bypassing the outbound's bind_interface/SO_MARK and looping back into the TUN. The fix copies SO_BINDTODEVICE and SO_MARK and binds the source address on the raw socket.
fork_evidence: Partial port in this round: `protocol/redirect` populates `OriginDestination`; the TLS-spoof raw-socket half is still open. Upstream: 9073ef8290f0.
notes: Fixed in this round; see docs/fork/upstream-2026-10-24-debug.md.

subject: Always compress DNS responses
root_cause: Responses were packed with Msg.Compress left false after unpacking, so every DNS response was encoded uncompressed; length budgets (512/EDNS0) and buffer sizing used the uncompressed length, so messages that would fit compressed were needlessly truncated (TC set, TCP fallback) or sent oversized over stream and Tailscale paths.
fork_evidence: Port in this round: the UDP truncation, stream writer and Tailscale peer-DNS reply pack compressed. `./dns` tests pass. Upstream: e2008d6b7dcb.
notes: Fixed in this round; see docs/fork/upstream-2026-10-24-debug.md.

subject: Fix WireGuard system device packet size on darwin
root_cause: systemDevice.Read copied the sing-tun device's return count straight into sizes[0], but that device reads through the offset-adjusted slice and reports its length including tun.PacketOffset, so wireguard-go was told each packet was 4 bytes longer than it is (the utun header). Upstream subtracts PacketOffset.
fork_evidence: Port in this round: the WireGuard system device subtracts `PacketOffset` from the read size. `./transport/wireguard` tests pass. Upstream: e352ada7ab45.
notes: Fixed in this round; see docs/fork/upstream-2026-10-24-debug.md.

subject: Fix IPv4 wildcard listen for experimental servers

Go's listen family selection turns a wildcard address into a dual-stack [::] socket, so an explicit 0.0.0.0:port bound IPv6 rather than the IPv4 wildcard the configuration named, or failed where IPv6 is unavailable. Upstream derives tcp4 from the parsed address.

subject: Follow resolved address order in parallel dial
root_cause: The parallel dialer chose its leading family from the raw domain_strategy option instead of the resolver's effective preference, so whenever the resolver preferred the other family the race started on the slower one and paid a fallback delay before trying the real answer.
fork_evidence: common/dialer/resolve.go:266-280 adopts the resolver's EffectiveStrategy from DNSFamilyResult instead of d.queryOptions.Strategy, and :380-395 feeds the preferred family first; DialParallelInterface (:941-945) documents the same fix, and dual_stack.go:158 plans from the effective strategy.
notes: The fork does not use addresses[0].Is6(); it keeps an effective-preference model (router default included) and interleaves families, so the wrong-family-first loss is removed by a different, documented mechanism.

subject: Stagger connection attempts in parallel dial
root_cause: The hand-rolled two-family racer attempted each family's candidates serially and duplicated N.DialParallel's policy; the fix consolidates on a scheduler that starts one candidate immediately and each further candidate after the fallback delay instead of launching all attempts at once.
fork_evidence: common/dialer/default_parallel_network.go:46-64 builds a candidate plan and :209 hands it to candidateScheduler.dial (dual_stack_scheduler.go:107-150), which starts the first candidate at once and one more per fallbackDelay (fallbackDelayOrDefault :625), advancing early on a definite failure.
notes: The commit also bumps sing to v0.9.7-0.20261023115510-03a6cce64bf7 for the N.DialParallel stagger; the fork replaces sing (go.mod:212) and only protocol/masque/client.go:881 still calls N.DialParallel, a separate inner-resolver race this change does not address.

subject: Fix direct outbound ignoring fallback delay
root_cause: The route layer calls the direct outbound's DialParallelNetwork with fallbackDelay 0 unless a route-action delay is set; forwarding 0 made the scheduler substitute the 300 ms default, silently discarding the outbound's configured fallback_delay.
fork_evidence: protocol/direct/outbound.go:311 forwards the argument unchanged, but its surface is the resolve wrapper: dialer.go:92-99 passes options.FallbackDelay to NewResolveDialer, and dual_stack_parallel_network.go:406-420 fallbackDelayOrDefaultFor() substitutes the dialer's configured delay whenever the caller passes 0.
notes: The configured direct fallback_delay is honoured through resolveParallelNetworkDialer; an explicit route delay still wins (route/route.go:730), so no explicit if-zero fallback in protocol/direct is needed.

subject: Fix URLTest session warmup for session-based outbounds
root_cause: URLTest issued its untimed warm request only when the detour advertised OutboundWithMultiplex; naive, tailscale and wireguard are session-based but did not advertise it, so their single timed request paid handshake and session setup and reported an inflated delay.
fork_evidence: common/urltest/measure.go:244 dials once and newMeasurementTransport (:31) hands that one conn to net/http, so Measure always sends an untimed HEAD and then the timed HEAD over the same warm connection. No fork code reads adapter.OutboundWithMultiplex.
notes: The fork's URLTest never consults MultiplexEnabled (route/failover.go:236 records that interface as having no consumer), so naive/tailscale/wireguard need no declaration; session warm-up is structural in Measure rather than opt-in.

subject: Exclude USB/IP from legacy Windows 7 build
root_cause: The legacy Windows 7 build row reused DEFAULT_BUILD_TAGS_OTHERS, which contains with_usbip. sing-usbip's Windows driver/cgo assets do not build with the patched Go 1.23 Windows 7 toolchain, so that release row failed; CI now strips with_usbip for the legacy row only.
fork_evidence: The fork has no .github/workflows/build.yml and no legacy_win7 matrix; its Windows build is windows-core-amd64.yml, which says at :19-23 that upstream's Windows 7 toolchain is deliberately not adopted and the artifact targets Windows 10/11 x64. Tag sets are fork-owned (release/DEFAULT_BUILD_TAGS_OTHERS, cmd/internal/build_libbox golden tags).
notes: No equivalent build row exists, so the CI edit has no target. The fork's supported Windows builds intentionally keep with_usbip on Windows 10/11.

subject: Enable ARM64 CPU feature detection in Windows builds
root_cause: Go's internal/cpu on windows/arm64 never initialises ARM64 feature flags before the CL 745560 backport, so crypto/aes, AES-GCM and sha256 use the generic Go implementations; the commit adds a toolchain patch and applies it to the Windows ARM64 build jobs.
fork_evidence: No windows/arm64 artifact is built: .github/workflows has windows-core-amd64.yml (amd64 only) and client-desktop-windows.yml (gate 3 asserts an amd64/x64 payload; release installer windows-x64); no build.yml and no windows CPU-feature patch. The only such patch is .github/go_ios_cpu_features.patch.
notes: Performance-only and toolchain-side; nothing in this tree performs windows/arm64 builds, so the patch would be dead. Revisit if such an artifact is added, or move to a Go release carrying golang/go#76791.

subject: Fix TLS sniffer storing IP literal server names as domain
root_cause: The TLS sniffer copied clientHello.ServerName verbatim into metadata.Domain. crypto/tls validates the SNI only structurally and filters IP literals only when sending, so a peer can put an IP literal or host:port there; a non-domain value in the domain plane then matches domain rules, pollutes logs/connections API and disables the direct fast path. The fix parses it as host:port and stores only .Fqdn.
fork_evidence: common/sniff/tls.go:114 already assigns metadata.Domain = M.ParseSocksaddrHostPort(clientHello.ServerName, 0).Fqdn, with the comment at :100-113 citing LX 19f57607 and explaining that a domain plane must only hold a domain; IP-literal and host:port normalisation is present.
notes: Identical to the upstream fix; no port needed. The fork's HTTP sniffer already used the same normalisation.

subject: Fix URL test failover for routed connections
root_cause: A failed dial through a URL-test group left the dead member's measurement intact, so the group kept ranking it best and later routed connections kept failing. The fix gives the connection manager the URL-test history store and deletes the failed chain leaf's entry whenever the chain contains an adapter.URLTestGroup.
fork_evidence: Port in this round: a failed connection through a URLTest group deletes the leaf's history. Test: `route/url_test_history_test.go`. Upstream: 5372a195b3ee.
notes: Fixed in this round; see docs/fork/upstream-2026-10-24-debug.md.
